applies_why: The judge text decides the Acts 2:30 point by treating the verse's silence about whose body is the channel as leaving the point open rather than weighing the two chains by footing.
quote: the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'by footing, never verse by verse': either the collision must be resolved by comparing the chains' support as chains, or a verse's silence can by itself leave the point open; I read K-C as requiring the former.
why: Because K-C retires the stating-verse test and requires chain-against-chain footing, the judge's underdetermination based on the verse not naming whose body is the channel breaches the rule.
